concepts.name: Relative judgment (softmax)
concepts.summary: Softmax over N candidate scores: p_i = e^(s_i) / sum_j e^(s_j) — exponentiate, then normalise so the weights sum to 1. A single COUPLED distribution in which only the gaps between scores matter (a common shift cancels), nudging any one score shifts every weight, and one candidate wins; with no rivals it is meaningless, since a lone candidate always gets p = 1. Answers 'which of these is best?'. Its regret for true candidate k is -log(p_k). (Upstairs it is CLIP's contrastive softmax cross-entropy over a batch of image-caption pairs — coupled, so training must all-gather across GPUs and craves ~32K batches for enough negatives.)

concepts.name: Binary cross-entropy (sigmoid)
concepts.summary: The regret for an INDEPENDENT yes/no verdict: -[y*log(p) + (1-y)*log(1-p)], where p = sigmoid(s) = 1/(1+e^(-s)) squashes a single score alone into (0,1). It is -log(p) when the truth is yes (y=1) and -log(1-p) when no (y=0). Each score is judged on its own absolute level with no denominator over rivals; a rescale t and shift b set the threshold, a negative b lowering every default probability when a 'yes' is rare. Changing one score leaves the other verdicts untouched. Answers 'is THIS one a yes?'. (Upstairs it is SigLIP's per-pair sigmoid loss — decoupled, no all-gather, small batches.)
